transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Morgan. I've completed my technology review of the proposed plan, and I have several important findings to share. First, personal phones cannot be used for school recordings — the project must use district tablets instead. Second, all source files must be stored in the restricted OralHistory drive, not on personal devices or general storage. Third, recordings must be deleted exactly 45 days after the final class presentation — indefinite retention as called for in the draft plan is not permitted. I want to clarify that storing source files in the restricted OralHistory drive does not prohibit publishing consented recordings on the public school website, so the public publication component can proceed for those interviewees who have consented, consistent with Mr. Lewis's consent-exclusion findings. Finally, the technology plan must include a secure-storage configuration record documenting these storage arrangements. This secure-storage configuration record will need to be included in the approval packet alongside the training-verification record and the consent-exclusion record. In summary, the draft plan requires four technology-related revisions before approval: use district tablets instead of personal phones, store source files in the restricted OralHistory drive, delete all recordings exactly 45 days after the final class presentation, and include a secure-storage configuration record in the approval packet.
